title: Sanctions against two major Russian oil companies are announced by the US
description_short: Sanctions against two major Russian oil companies are announced by the US Treasury and the European Union
description_medium: On October 22, 2025, the U.S. Treasury imposed sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil, two major Russian oil companies, and more than 30 of their majority-owned subsidiaries. The European Union announced a broader sanctions package the next day. Both moves aimed to pressure Moscow toward a ceasefire in Ukraine; the U.S. measures blocked covered property and restricted dealings with the companies.
description_long: On October 22, 2025, the U.S. Treasury announced sanctions targeting Rosneft and Lukoil, two of Russia’s largest oil companies, along with more than 30 majority-owned subsidiaries. The U.S. measures block covered property under U.S. jurisdiction and require it to be reported to the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control; violations can bring civil or criminal penalties. The Treasury said the steps would constrain revenue supporting Russia’s war effort. The European Union announced a separate, broader package the following day, its 19th, covering energy, military, and financial sectors. It included a future ban on Russian liquefied natural gas imports, restrictions on maritime services for designated oil vessels, and measures against other entities. Washington and Brussels described the sanctions as pressure on Moscow to end its war against Ukraine and move toward a ceasefire. Trump said he had waited a long time before acting and had canceled a planned meeting with Vladimir Putin because it did not seem likely to advance negotiations. The announcements expanded economic pressure but did not themselves establish that a ceasefire had been reached.
